name: Vello paints the board canvas and motion lives in the painter
summary: A page paints a picture on a canvas with Vello, on WebGPU or the CPU, and the painter's stage holds all picture motion in Rust, so the DOM motion modules go and the SVG stays as the semantic layer and the export.

value.name: Painter stage
value.responsibility: Holds one canvas's picture, how it is seen and everything that moves on it, and draws a frame of it for the time a host gives
value.description: The host hands it a picture, how the picture arrives, the camera, the light, the far view, the marks and the traffic. It also holds the sweeps, the warnings and the traffic clock. Everything that changes over time is worked out from the clock the host gives, so a stepped clock records it frame by frame.

value.label: a whole picture's move, as a flight
draw each frame's items
what lies under a point

value.name: Picture motion
value.responsibility: Turns one scene into the next as a pure function of a progress value: it pairs groups by subject id and mixes their typed geometry, opacity and transforms
value.description: The entrance, the departure, the far swap and the flight into a card follow the same rule. Nothing here draws, reads a clock or keeps state between frames, so the same inputs give the same items. The durations come from @archboard/timing through the page. flight.rs holds what moves a whole picture: a flight from the last picture, a part-by-part entrance, a leaving picture, the ghost of one that left, and the board inside a card that the camera flies into.

value.name: Canvas drawing
value.responsibility: Walks a scene under its presentation and draws it on a Canvas, with the theme's palette, the glyph outlines and the CPU canvas on vello_cpu
value.description: It does what the SVG's stylesheet did: the colours of a theme, the recede of a lit set, the far view and the order in which a selected part is raised. A glyph is drawn from the outlines of the core's own faces. Vello on the GPU implements the same Canvas trait in the browser crate.

value.name: Scene picking
value.responsibility: Answers what lies under a point from the scene, in the order the painter draws, under the rules of SVG pointer-events
value.description: A shape takes the pointer where it is painted, and an invisible stroke counts, because a line's wide halo is what makes it easy to hit. The flow heads that the page holds count where they are drawn.

value.name: Painter choice
value.responsibility: Chooses the painter of a canvas once, from what the browser says: Vello on WebGPU when it gives a real adapter and a device, Vello on the CPU otherwise
value.description: A software adapter, or none, sends the canvas to the CPU painter, and the rule reads no frame back. If the GPU fails to start or in a frame, the CPU painter takes over on a fresh canvas, because a canvas that held a WebGPU context never takes a 2D one. The caller shows which painter draws, and why the GPU does not.

value.label: start the GPU or the CPU painter

changes.value: A replay swaps it once, before it mounts anything. Its stepped clock runs frame callbacks and timers at their due times, and takes over the browser's own requestAnimationFrame, so a library's frames run on it too. It pauses and stands every Web Animation and CSS transition at the frame's time, and records a violation for an animation on a timeline it cannot stand. The picture stage draws its frames from it. A lint rule keeps the viewer and the subtitles on it.

It tells the stage how the picture arrives, cut to, carried on from the last or brought in part by part, and how far the cards the two pictures share have moved; the painter does the motion. Flights read the time and their frames from the frame clock. The picture of a board that a flight into a card arrived at is put up as it is, with no entrance.

changes.value:
It mounts the recording page's stage, viewer and subtitles, and no workbench, pane session or socket, so no Codex is involved. Loading a talk plays the board's entrance through first, uncaptured, so frame 0 shows the board at rest. A frame is ready once the fonts are loaded, no read is in flight, no painter is still starting, the step's picture is drawn and the page has not changed for two turns of its event loop, within RECORDING_FRAME_READY_MS. The stepped clock runs even the frames a library asks of the browser, and stands every animation at the frame's time. An animation on another timeline, or a read of another board, fails the render and names the frame.

A canonical talk draws its captured model and narrative through the shared walkthrough presentation. It reads no mutable vault and needs no source repository for replay.

value.label: wait for the painter to start

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/UOXNWLhR#XXTC3G6Y
changes.value: A replay swaps it once, before it mounts anything (driveFramesFrom). Its stepped clock also takes over the browser's own requestAnimationFrame, so a library's frames run on it too. It stands every animation at the frame's time. An animation on a timeline it cannot stand is a violation. The picture stage asks it for its frames and reads its time, so a replay steps the canvas too. A lint rule keeps the viewer on it rather than on the browser's timers.

value.name: Picture stage
value.responsibility: Owns the canvas of one surface and its painter, hands the painter what the page says, and asks the frame clock for frames only while something moves
value.description: Until the painter's first frame the surface shows the SVG with its ink, and a painter that cannot start leaves it so: a correct board. The SVG stays in the page under the canvas as the hidden semantic layer that search, copy, screen readers and the marks read, written by picture-transition.ts. picture-ink.ts keeps a first picture's ink back for a moment so that the painter brings the picture in. React gives the stage a host, and the stage makes each canvas inside it, so a painter that fails is released and a replacement gets a fresh canvas. picture-ink.ts then gives the SVG back the glyphs and definitions that a painted surface dropped, so complete ink shows while the replacement starts. The surface says which painter draws in data-painter, and why the GPU does not in data-painter-reason.

value.label: start the painter of this canvas

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/vKEsyHFk#OHywsFXm
changes.value: The TypeScript hosts in this package load the renderer core, which crates/ builds to WebAssembly (ADR 0059). The core measures, lays out and paints. A host runs its layout solves and gives it icons and theme colours. A page paints a picture on a canvas with Vello, on WebGPU or on the CPU, from the same scene. The SVG stays the product of exports, PNGs and README assets, and stays in the page as the semantic layer. Recordings paint on the CPU.

value.name: Picture pick
value.responsibility: Says what lies under an event in the picture: the painter answers while one works, and the event answers otherwise
value.description: With a painter at work the surface takes no pointer, so the painter picks from the scene. An event that reached a group of the picture all the same came from no pointer: assistive technology clicks the group it found, and the event names it.

value.label: the painter that answers

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/UOXNWLhR#oF5Ib5A4
changes.value: The way, the card's box in the leaving picture when the reader went into one, and the board drawn next. The stage sends the picture on its way out: it zooms into an opened card, draws away going back, else fades.

value.name: Painter core
value.responsibility: Draws a typed scene on a canvas and works out every move from one picture to the next, as plain Rust with no DOM and no GPU of its own
value.description: One Canvas trait serves Vello on the GPU and Vello on the CPU, so both run the same walk over the scene (ADR 0071). The in-between of two scenes is a pure function of the scenes and a progress value, so Rust tests own it. A host tells the stage what changed and what time it is, and asks for frames.

value.name: Browser painter
value.responsibility: The Painter class that a page holds: one stage and the canvas its frames land on, painted by Vello on WebGPU or by Vello on the CPU
value.description: A page asks it to show, carry, enter, leave or dive a picture, to set the camera, the light and the marks, to pick under a point and to draw a frame for a time. This crate is a browser's: a native build of the workspace compiles it empty. It carries the hash of the sources it was built from, and the page refuses a build of other sources.

value.label: one stage for the canvas
